blocks.value: Every program you have written lives entirely inside `main`. That works until it doesn't, around fifty lines, `main` becomes something nobody can read, including you next week.
Methods fix that, and they are also the bridge to everything in the Intermediate tier. A class is mostly a collection of methods, so this lesson is where object-oriented Java quietly begins.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Use the `Math` class for common calculations
Write value-returning methods and void methods
Explain the parts of a method heading
Describe how Java passes arguments by value
